note: AI summary written on the ground from the simulator figures only (src/sim, Mouad's data). To be validated by the CMO. Never used to decide on an alert.

days.text: Baseline assessment (D0): VO₂max of 44.1 ml/kg/min, ejection fraction of 61.8%. Good endurance capacity before departure. Status: nominal.
VO₂max at 42.2 ml/kg/min, i.e. 95.7% of preflight. The decline (about −0.8 per week) is expected early in flight. Ejection fraction stable at 61.9%.
VO₂max at 40.6 ml/kg/min, i.e. 92.2% of preflight. Ventricular mass at 96.8% of D0: the heart is adapting to microgravity. Still above the NASA thresholds.

VO₂max at 39.3 ml/kg/min, i.e. 89.2% of preflight: status: monitor. Above both NASA thresholds (80% of preflight [V1 4003] and 36.5 ml/kg/min [V1 4002]), but the slope leads right to the limit on arrival at Mars. Suggested action: cycle or treadmill intervals every other day.
Projection at Sol 0 (D210) at current pace: VO₂max of 36.5 ml/kg/min (83% of preflight). This is exactly the NASA threshold of 36.5 [V1 4002]: status: monitor. Model projection, not a measurement.
Projection at Sol 0 (D210) with the plan followed: VO₂max of 37.3 ml/kg/min (84.8% of preflight). This is above the 36.5 threshold [V1 4002]: status: monitor. Model projection, not a measurement.

Projection at return (D860) at current pace: VO₂max of 34.5 ml/kg/min, i.e. 78.4% of preflight. This is below both NASA thresholds [V1 4002, V1 4003]: status out of limits. Model projection, not a measurement.

Projection at return (D860) with the plan followed: VO₂max of 35.9 ml/kg/min, i.e. 81.6% of preflight. This is above 80% of preflight [V1 4003] but below 36.5 [V1 4002]: status out of limits. The plan protects endurance but is not enough over 860 days.
